Single-cell: expression across groups

Source: vignettes/articles/sc-expression.Rmd
sc-expression.Rmd

Question: which genes mark each group of cells, and how does a gene’s expression differ between groups or conditions?

Function Shows Best for
top_markers() the top genes of each group from a marker table choosing features
DotPlot_bioToolkit() % of cells expressing (size) and mean expression (colour) many genes × groups
VlnPlot_bioToolkit() per-cell distributions, with box and points a few genes or QC metrics
RidgePlot_bioToolkit() per-cell distributions as density ridges shapes of distributions, many groups
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit() expression of each cell or group mean, z-scored marker blocks, conditions within cell types

All share group.by (the groups compared, marked by their colour) and split.by (a higher-level grouping drawn as labelled blocks): group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type" compares conditions within each cell type. Note that Seurat’s DotPlot() / VlnPlot() use split.by the other way round.

Blocks (split.by, and groups of genes given as a named list) are marked the same way in every plot: a bar along the block, 3.5 pt thick (group.bar.width), set a little off the grid, with the block’s name beyond it. Bars are black by default; split.by.cols and feature.group.cols colour them (a palette name, or colours named by block). They sit opposite the axis labels by default (gene groups on top when genes are the columns); "labels" in split.by.side / feature.group.side moves them beyond the labels.

Data: 8,000 PBMCs from Kang et al. 2018, control or interferon-β (IFN-β) stimulated, with the authors’ cell types. Gene symbols are human (upper case, e.g. CD3E).

pbmc <- docs_kang()

Marker genes

top_markers() reads a marker table (Seurat’s FindAllMarkers() or any DE table with a group column) and returns the top genes of each group as a named list, the features format of the dot plot and heatmap. With unique = TRUE (default), a gene that marks several groups is kept for the group where its fold change is largest.

markers <- Seurat::FindAllMarkers(
    pbmc,
    only.pos = TRUE,
    logfc.threshold = 0.5,
    min.pct = 0.1,
    verbose = FALSE
)
top <- top_markers(markers, n = 3)
str(top)
#> List of 8
#>  $ CD4 T        : chr [1:3] "LEF1" "ADTRP" "TSHZ2"
#>  $ CD8 T        : chr [1:3] "GZMH" "KLRG1" "LAG3"
#>  $ NK           : chr [1:3] "SH2D1B" "KLRF1" "LINC00996"
#>  $ B            : chr [1:3] "MS4A1" "LINC00926" "CD79A-ENSG00000105369"
#>  $ CD14 Mono    : chr [1:3] "SERPINB2" "S100A8" "S100A9"
#>  $ FCGR3A Mono  : chr [1:3] "VMO1" "CASP5" "CH25H"
#>  $ DC           : chr [1:3] "DNASE1L3" "FSCN1" "FCER1A"
#>  $ Megakaryocyte: chr [1:3] "GP9" "CLDN5" "PTCRA"

rank.by = "logfc" (default) favours genes specific to a group; rank.by = "padj" favours broadly and strongly expressed genes, as p-values grow with group size:

str(top_markers(markers, n = 3, rank.by = "padj")[1:3])
#> List of 3
#>  $ CD4 T: chr [1:3] "LTB-ENSG00000227507" "SELL" "LDHB"
#>  $ CD8 T: chr [1:3] "GZMH" "CD8A" "LAG3"
#>  $ NK   : chr [1:3] "GNLY" "CLIC3" "PRF1"

Per-cell tests (as FindAllMarkers()) treat cells as replicates: fine to rank markers, but their p-values are not evidence for differences between conditions; use pseudobulk tests for that (see DE: many comparisons).

Dot plot 

DotPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = top, group.by = "cell_type")

By default, each gene’s mean expression is z-scored across groups (scale), so colours compare groups for a gene, not genes with each other. The colour scale is centred on 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own most extreme value (at most ±2.5), so it need not be symmetric. Groups are marked with the cell type colours of DimPlot_bioToolkit(); the groups of genes by bars on top.

Variants

Interferon-stimulated genes in each condition (group.by, the dot colours), within each cell type (split.by, the blocks, named on the right):

isg <- c("ISG15", "IFI6", "IFIT1", "MX1", "CXCL10")
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = isg,
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)

The gene groups take the cell type colours, and both groupings move beyond the labels ("labels"):

cell_cols <- bt_palette("scanpy-20", nlevels(pbmc$cell_type))
names(cell_cols) <- levels(pbmc$cell_type)
DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top[1:4],
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A"),
    feature.group.cols = cell_cols,
    feature.group.side = "labels",
    split.by.cols = cell_cols,
    split.by.side = "labels"
)

Unscaled mean expression (log-normalized), comparable between genes:

DotPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = isg, group.by = "cell_type", scale = FALSE)

Genes as rows, groups as columns (the gene groups then on the right); group.marker = "strip" draws colour strips instead of dots:

DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top[1:4],
    group.by = "cell_type",
    flip = TRUE,
    group.marker = "strip"
)

Order genes (within each gene group) and groups by hierarchical clustering:

DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = unlist(top, use.names = FALSE),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    cluster.features = TRUE,
    cluster.groups = TRUE
)

average = "linear" (default, as Seurat) is the log of the mean normalized expression, a pseudobulk; "log" (as SCpubr) the mean of log values, less driven by a few very high cells. pct.min hides dots of groups with few expressing cells:

DotPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    average = "log",
    pct.min = 5
)

Violin plot 

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = c("CD14", "LYZ"), group.by = "cell_type")

Each feature has its own panel and axis; points are a random sample of at most pt.n cells per violin, rasterized.

Variants

Metadata columns work like genes, from the object or from a data frame of per-cell values. log puts chosen features on a log10 axis:

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc[[]],
    features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA"),
    group.by = "sample",
    log = TRUE,
    flip = TRUE,
    pt.n = 300
)

Sparse genes: most cells have 0 counts. zeros = "annotate" draws the violins of the cells above 0 and prints the % of cells above 0, so that both the fraction expressing and the level are visible. The cell type blocks are marked by bars in their colours (split.by.cols):

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    zeros = "annotate",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A"),
    split.by.cols = cell_cols
)

Many genes as thin rows sharing the group axis; pt.n = 0 draws no points:

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("CD3E", "NKG7", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A", "PPBP"),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    stack = TRUE,
    pt.n = 0
)

Zoom past a few extreme cells ("q99": the 99th percentile). The violins and boxes are computed from all cells and cut at the top of the axis; points above it are not drawn:

VlnPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "nCount_RNA",
    group.by = "cell_type",
    y.max = "q99"
)

Ridge plot

The same data arguments as the violin plot, drawn as density ridges. Each ridge is scaled to its own height, so ridges compare shapes, not cell numbers; overlap sets how far they overlap.

RidgePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("ISG15", "nFeature_RNA"),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    overlap = 1.5
)

RidgePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    group.by = "cell_type",
    zeros = "annotate",
    cells = colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$condition == "IFN-beta"]
)

Heatmap

Genes as rows, in blocks of the features list, each marked by a bar opposite the gene names; columns are cells (at most max.cells per group, so that small groups stay visible), z-scored per gene, in blocks named on top. Any gene of the assay can be drawn, not only those in scale.data.

DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top_markers(markers, n = 5),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100
)

Variants

One column per group mean: here conditions (dots) within cell types (blocks). Group means use a light-centred diverging palette:

heat_genes <- list(
    "IFN-stimulated" = isg,
    "Markers" = c("CD3E", "MS4A1", "CD14")
)
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = heat_genes,
    group.by = "condition",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    columns = "groups",
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)

Blocks of genes and of columns in the cell type colours (feature.group.cols, split.by.cols):

DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top_markers(markers, n = 4),
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100,
    group.marker = "none",
    feature.group.cols = cell_cols,
    split.by.cols = cell_cols
)

Further metadata as colour strips above the columns, e.g. the donor of each cell:

mono <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type == "CD14 Mono"]
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = isg,
    cells = mono,
    group.by = "condition",
    annotations = "donor",
    max.cells = 150,
    group.cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)

For many genes, names are hidden when rows are too thin; name a few with leader lines:

top20 <- top_markers(markers, n = 20)
first_genes <- vapply(top20, `[`, "", 1)   # first gene of each group
DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = top20,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    max.cells = 100,
    label.features = first_genes
)
